data.description:
The scheduled **Reconcile Bridge** GitHub Action (and the Reconciler Heartbeat Canary)
fails every run on live `navapbc/rebar` since 2026-08-15T02:39Z. ACLI aborts the inbound
fetch with:

`✗ Error: failed to parse JQL query: the value 'leg' does not exist for the field 'project'`
on JQL `project = LEG AND status != "Done"`, so `reconcile_once` raises and the pass exits 1.

## Root cause

The live `tickets` branch's `.bridge_state/projects.json` was overwritten with the
multi-project **rehearsal fixture** mapping — keys `LEG`/`ONE`/`TWO`/`ZERO` (repos
`rebar-legacy`/`rebar`/`rebar-web,rebar-api`/none), `legacy_default: null` — none of which
exist in the live REB Jira Cloud. The story-1734 multi-project fan-out
(`fetcher._build_snapshot`: `project_list = list(read_projects().keys()) or [_query_project]`)
issues `jql_active(proj)` for EVERY mapped key; the first, `project = LEG …`, is
syntactically valid (passes `_PROJECT_KEY_RE`) but Jira rejects it because project LEG does
not exist → ACLI exit 1 → whole pass fails.

The corruption landed as ad-hoc `git commit` calls on the live tickets branch
(`9f1b2cff98` "commit mapping" + `275bd7507e` "scrub", authored `t <t@t.co>` — the
test-fixture git identity) at 2026-08-14T19:18-0700 (=08-15T02:18Z), 21 min before the first
consistent failure. The known-good green-run state (commit `0d9f4b8459`) was
`{legacy_default: "REB", projects: {}}` — empty projects → fan-out falls back to the single
configured project REB.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The live `origin/tickets:.bridge_state/projects.json` is restored to the canonical
  single-project state `{"version": 1, "legacy_default": "REB", "projects": {}}` (byte-identical
  to the ensure-registry seed), removing the nonexistent LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO keys.
- [ ] A live `rebar bridge preview` against REB runs without the JQL parse error (no
  `project = LEG` query is issued) — verified by command output.
- [ ] The next scheduled Reconcile Bridge run completes green (verified via `gh run view`).

## Testing

- Reproduce the fan-out locally: `python3 -c "from rebar_reconciler.fetcher import jqls_for; print(jqls_for('LEG'))"`
  shows the failing `project = LEG AND status != "Done"` query.
- Verify the repair with `rebar bridge preview` (read-only; no Jira writes) against live REB.
- Confirm the scheduled `Reconcile Bridge` workflow run goes green.
data.title: Reconcile Bridge broken: rehearsal projects.json (LEG/ONE/TWO/ZERO) leaked to live tickets branch
